capabilities: Collect unstructured materials (worksheets, recordings, photos, videos) into project/action folders
Transcribe audio and video and describe images with AI models
Extract evidence against teaching goals and generate action, project, and term reports
Produce internal and redacted external report versions with aliases and blurred photos
Sync recordings from Dedao and export reports as PDF
disambiguation: Not a literacy-instruction tool; it is an assessment workbench that turns collected classroom materials into AI-organized evidence reports.
extras: Free for individual tutors; institutional or commercial use requires written authorization from the PBL-EDU project team. Detailed usage and architecture docs are linked separately. The README states the full workflow has not yet been verified end-to-end with real API keys, and known limits include a 25 MB per-file transcription cap, no manual evidence review UI, and no PDF/Word parsing.
problem: Obsidian has no structured workflow for project-based student assessment: gathering lesson materials, extracting evidence with AI against teaching goals, and producing per-student or term reports with a privacy-redacted version.
